t.5.2.1: Having crossed the unassailable ocean, that mighty one, at ease and unwearied, beheld Laṅkā standing upon the summit of Trikūṭa.
t.5.2.2: Then the mighty one, standing there showered with a rain of flowers released by the trees, shone as though he were made of flowers.
t.5.2.3: Though he had crossed a hundred yojanas, the glorious monkey of supreme valor, not even panting, felt no weariness there.
t.5.2.4: I could stride across many hundreds of yojanas; how much more, then, the far shore of the ocean, reckoned at a hundred yojanas!
t.5.2.5: But he, the foremost of the mighty and the best among leapers, swift in his speed, crossed over the great ocean and went to Laṅkā.
t.5.2.6: He went through the midst of dark-green grassy meadows and fragrant forests, through tracts strewn with boulders and tracts covered with trees.
t.5.2.7: The radiant Hanumān, bull among leaping monkeys, strode across mountains covered with trees and through rows of flowering forests.
t.5.2.8: Standing upon that mountain, the son of the Wind beheld the forests and the groves, and from the mountain's summit he beheld that Laṅkā.
t.5.2.9: He beheld sarala pines, karṇikāras and date palms in full bloom, priyālas and muculindas, kuṭajas and ketakas as well.
t.5.2.11: He saw trees bound with a burden of flowers and others also in bud, swarming with birds, their tops shaken by the wind.
t.5.2.10: He saw priyaṅgu trees laden with fragrance, nīpas and saptacchadas as well, and asanas, kovidāras and karavīras in full bloom.
t.5.2.12: He saw ponds thronged with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks and filled with lotuses and water lilies, many kinds of delightful pleasure gardens, and many kinds of lakes.
t.5.2.14: And having approached Laṅkā, protected by Rāvaṇa, the glorious one beheld it adorned with moats filled with lotuses and water-lilies.
t.5.2.13: The elephant among monkeys beheld them thickly covered with diverse trees bearing fruit and flowers in every season, and he saw delightful gardens as well.
t.5.2.16: He beheld the delightful great city, encircled by a golden rampart, crowded with hundreds of watchtowers and garlanded with banners and flags.
t.5.2.15: He saw the city, closely guarded by Rāvaṇa because of his abduction of Sītā, and by rākṣasas with fearsome bows who roamed about on every side.
t.5.2.17: Hanumān beheld Laṅkā, adorned with heavenly golden archways variegated with rows of creepers, like a city of the gods in heaven.
t.5.2.18: That glorious monkey beheld Laṅkā, standing on the mountain's summit with its beautiful white mansions, like a city moving through the sky.
t.5.2.19: Hanumān beheld the city, guarded by the lord of the Rākṣasas and built by Viśvakarman, seeming as if it floated in the sky.
t.5.2.20: The city, filled with fierce Rākṣasas as Bhogavatī is with Nāgas, beyond imagining, finely built and plainly visible, was once the dwelling of Kubera.
t.5.2.21: It was guarded by many fearsome, valiant, fanged rākṣasas bearing tridents and paṭṭiśas in their hands, like a cave guarded by venomous serpents.
t.5.2.22: Her hips were the ramparts and walls, her fresh garment the abundant waters, the ends of her tresses the śataghnīs and spears, and her ear-ornaments the watchtowers.
t.5.2.23: Reaching the northern gate, which looked like a peak of Kailāsa and seemed to scrape the sky, the monkey reflected, while the heavens appeared to be held aloft by the lofty, splendid mansions.
t.5.2.24: Having observed its mighty defenses and the ocean, and Rāvaṇa, the terrible enemy, the monkey fell to thinking.
t.5.2.25: Even if the monkeys come here, they will be of no avail, for Laṅkā cannot be conquered in battle even by the gods.
t.5.2.26: But even if he reaches this Laṅkā, rugged and hard to approach, guarded by Rāvaṇa, what will that mighty-armed Rāghava do?
t.5.2.27: Among the rākṣasas no opening is found for conciliation, nor for gifts, nor for sowing dissension; not even for war is any scope to be seen.
t.5.2.28: Indeed, only four of the great-souled monkeys have the power to reach this place: the son of Vālin, Nīla, I myself, and the wise king.
t.5.2.29: Until I know whether Vaidehī is alive or not, and until I have seen that daughter of Janaka, I shall consider only that matter.
t.5.2.30: Then that elephant among monkeys, standing on that mountain peak and devoted to the success of Rāma, reflected for a moment.
t.5.2.31: In this form I cannot enter the city of the Rākṣasas, guarded as it is by cruel Rākṣasas endowed with great strength.
t.5.2.32: The rākṣasas are of fierce energy, great valour and mighty strength; all of them must be eluded by me as I search for Jānakī.
t.5.2.34: Seeing that city of such a kind, unassailable even by the Suras and Asuras, Hanumān sighed again and again and fell to thinking.
t.5.2.33: At night the city of Laṅkā must be entered by me in a form now visible, now invisible. The time has come for me to accomplish my great task.
t.5.2.35: By what means might I see Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, while remaining unseen by Rāvaṇa, the evil-minded lord of the rākṣasas?
t.5.2.36: How may the task of Rāma, whose self is known, not come to ruin? I alone should see Janaka's daughter alone, in a secluded place.
t.5.2.37: Even matters already accomplished come to ruin when they run counter to place and time, or when they fall into the hands of a bewildered messenger, just as darkness perishes at the rising of the sun.
t.5.2.38: In a matter poised between gain and loss, even a firm resolve does not shine forth; for messengers who fancy themselves learned bring ruin upon their tasks.
t.5.2.39: How can the task not be ruined, and how can confusion not arise? And how indeed can my leap across the ocean not be in vain?
t.5.2.40: But if I am seen by the rākṣasas, this mission of the wise Rāma, who desires the ruin of Rāvaṇa, would come to nothing.
t.5.2.41: For it is not possible to stay anywhere unnoticed by the Rākṣasas, even in the form of a Rākṣasa; how much less in any other form!
t.5.2.42: It is my belief that even the wind could not move here unknown, for nothing escapes the knowledge of the mighty Rākṣasas.
t.5.2.43: If I remain here clothed in my own form, I shall meet with destruction, and my master's purpose will be lost.
t.5.2.45: Entering by night the city of Rāvaṇa, so very hard to approach, and searching every dwelling, I shall find the daughter of Janaka.
t.5.2.44: Therefore, having shrunk my own form to smallness, I shall descend upon Laṅkā in the night for the accomplishment of Rāghava's purpose.
t.5.2.46: Having reflected thus, the heroic monkey Hanumān, eager to see Vaidehī, then awaited the setting of the sun. Making himself no bigger than a cat, he became wondrous to behold.
t.5.2.47: At the time of dusk, the valiant Hanumān swiftly leapt up and entered the delightful city, whose great highways were well laid out.
t.5.2.49: He beheld the great city with its seven-storeyed and eight-storeyed mansions, whose floors were inlaid with crystal and adorned with gold.
t.5.2.48: The city lay spread with rows of palaces, with pillars of gold and silver and with lattices wrought of gold, like a city of the Gandharvas.
t.5.2.50: There the mansions of the Rākṣasas shone with their floors variegated with vaiḍūrya gems and adorned with networks of pearls.
t.5.2.51: The variegated golden archways of the Rākṣasas lit up Laṅkā, which was adorned on every side.
t.5.2.52: Having beheld Laṅkā, inconceivable and of wondrous form, the great monkey was at once dejected and delighted, eager for the sight of Vaidehī.
t.5.2.53: He beheld the city of the illustrious ones, garlanded with rows of white, lofty mansions, its gateways adorned with costly latticework of Jāmbūnada gold, protected by the arms of Rāvaṇa and surrounded by night-roaming Rākṣasas of fearsome strength.
t.5.2.54: The moon too, as if rendering him assistance, rose with its many thousands of rays, shining in the midst of the hosts of stars and spreading a canopy of moonlight over the world.
t.5.2.55: That foremost of monkeys beheld the moon rising and shining forth, lustrous as a conch, white as milk and lotus fibres, like a swan gliding upon a lake.
